evidence: src/application/catalogue-service.ts: CatalogueService(products: ProductRepository) handles product use cases. addProduct delegates creation to Product.create and returns product.snapshot().

src/application/order-service.ts: OrderService(orders, products, ids, clock) handles order use cases and delegates rules to Order.place/advanceTo/cancel and Product.ensureAvailable/reserve/dispatch/release.
Both services return snapshots (ProductSnapshot, OrderSnapshot) and save changes only through injected repository ports, so neither skips the module's own abstractions.

Minor overlap: CatalogueService.getProduct and OrderService.requireProduct both run products.findById and throw NotFoundError(`Product ${id} not found`). This is a small piece of repeated lookup code, not a duplicated business invariant.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files serve one concern: application-layer use-case services that orchestrate domain aggregates through repository ports. They use the same patterns throughout. Each service has a constructor that injects domain interfaces (ProductRepository, OrderRepository, IdGenerator, Clock). Inputs are command interfaces (AddProductCommand, PlaceOrderCommand), and every result is returned as a domain snapshot (ProductSnapshot, OrderSnapshot) rather than the aggregate itself. Business rules are left to the domain objects: Product.create, ensureAvailable, reserve, dispatch and release, plus Order.place, advanceTo and cancel. Neither service changes state directly or skips a repository. The only overlap is the product lookup that throws NotFoundError(`Product ${id} not found`). It appears in both CatalogueService.getProduct and OrderService.requireProduct. This is a small piece of repeated lookup-and-throw code, not a business invariant duplicated across the unit, so it falls short of the Fail bar. The empty-order check in placeOrder might repeat a check inside Order.place, but that code is not visible here, so I can't confirm it.
